<details>
The PKGBUILD's global (top-level) scope consists only of ordinary variable assignments: `pkgname`, `_repo`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `options`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. There are no top-level command substitutions, no `$(...)` or backtick execution, no `eval`/`base64`/`curl`/`wget` calls, and no file or system modifications that would run while the PKGBUILD is sourced for `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

The `source` array points to the package's own declared upstream repository (`git+https://github.com/sweetwm/sweetbg.git`) and `sha256sums` is `SKIP`, which is normal for a VCS `-git` package and is irrelevant to this gate since no sources are fetched during `--printsrcinfo`. The remaining code lives inside `pkgver()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()`, which are not executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and are therefore out of scope for this specific check. Nothing in the sourced scope downloads or runs untrusted payloads or exfiltrates data.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Top-level scope has only normal variable assignments; no execution risk.</summary>
</security_assessment>

The `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions run the upstream meson/ninja build system and install files only into `$pkgdir` via `meson install` and `install -Dm644` (README and example config). There are no network downloads beyond the declared git source, no `git pull`/`git fetch` + `reset --hard` in prepare/build, no `curl|bash`, no base64/obfuscated payloads, no `eval`, no access to credentials, `/etc/shadow`, SSH keys, or arbitrary file exfiltration, and no system modifications outside the package directory. Nothing deviates from routine packaging practice.
</details>
